newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end up on thin institutional buying.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end up on thin institutional buying.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks ended Thursday on a marginally firmer note, after being down for much of the afternoon, as foreign institutional buy programs fizzled out, dealers said.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 1.16 points to 1,224.94, while the broader EMAS index was up just 0.19 to 345.26.
"We have been buying Tenaga, Sime Darby and other blue chip stocks for our foreign clients today, but not in particularly big volumes," said a trader at a foreign brokerage house in Kuala Lumpur.
The small-cap Second Board index was nearly flat at 0.35 points down to 563.87
"Usually following a buy program, there will be a sell program, which is why we have been seeing some selling of blue-chips as well," said William Chan, an institutional trader at Jupiter Securities.
Volume remained thin, with 170 million shares traded, valued at 1,225 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 289 to 259.
Advanced Synergy was the day's most actively-traded stock again, on talk of a possible bank deal. The stock was up 20 cents to 4.64 ringgit.
